version.author: Pontaku Audio
version.changelog:
SoundPrep 0.11.14
This is an upkeep release for the native helper. The helper now updates itself, waveform peaks finish building at selection, and the Windows native windows finally match REAPER.
Helper auto-update: when a SoundPrep update brings a newer helper, launching SoundPrep swaps it in automatically and asks you to restart REAPER, the same flow as other ReaPack extensions. No more copying the DLL or dylib by hand. If the swap is not possible, SoundPrep falls back to the manual instructions. This release requires the new helper, and the automatic update handles it. Just restart REAPER when asked.
Waveform peaks: for typical sources (up to about two minutes of stereo, longer in proportion for fewer channels), peaks now build to completion as soon as you select the file, instead of finishing partway into playback. Longer and multichannel sources get a large head start and complete moments later.
Windows windows: the bar, App Settings, Microphones and Preset Editor windows now all use the classic dialog surface REAPER itself uses, so backgrounds no longer differ between a window, its tabs and its text. This replaces the 0.11.13 unification, which did not fully take on Windows.
SoundPrep is free and open source. If it saves you time, you can support development on Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/kuma_pontakuaudio

version.author: Pontaku Audio
version.changelog:
SoundPrep 0.11.15
The tracks SoundPrep adds for its preview chains are now named SoundPrep instead of AM, the old AuditionMacro name. The input track, the Raw track and each chain track now read SoundPrep • Preview input, SoundPrep • Raw and SoundPrep • followed by the chain name.
Existing projects keep working exactly as before, because SoundPrep recognises its tracks by an internal marker, not by name. Saved projects keep their current track names; new projects get the new ones.
SoundPrep is free and open source. If it saves you time, you can support development on Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/kuma_pontakuaudio

SoundPrep 0.11.16
Fixed the channel waveform display switching back and forth with REAPER's own waveform while using Mic Select. When a channel selection restarts the preview, the selected channels' waveform now stays on screen instead of flickering between the two displays.
SoundPrep is free and open source. If it saves you time, you can support development on Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/kuma_pontakuaudio

version.author: Pontaku Audio
version.changelog:
SoundPrep 0.11.17
Fixed the selected-channel waveform overlay not appearing on macOS when REAPER's GPU acceleration is enabled. The overlay is now drawn in its own window on macOS, so it stays visible with GPU acceleration (Metal) on and no setting change is needed. If the overlay window cannot be used, SoundPrep now shows a notice in the bar explaining the GPU acceleration setting to change.
SoundPrep is free and open source. If it saves you time, you can support development on Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/kuma_pontakuaudio

version.author: Pontaku Audio
version.changelog:
SoundPrep 0.11.18
SoundPrep now renders through drops. Use Render selected drops to bake an existing Source + FX drop. The preset tail still applies when rendering with handles. Removed the standalone Export settings for final normalization, true-peak limiting, and the limiter ceiling.
Waveform peaks for channel selections and multichannel files are now built by SoundPrep's own peak store. Builds are no longer paced, so the waveform completes sooner, and finished peaks are cached for the session, so selecting a file again shows its waveform right away. Very large files (over 200 million samples) keep using REAPER's peak building.
If REAPER refuses to restore an item after a failed render, SoundPrep reports both errors, attempts to restore the remaining items, and closes the undo block. Queued renders also clear their busy flag.
